name: Gamco Ltd
title: Gamco Ltd - 540097 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GAMCO H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 79% to INR254 crore and net profit reached INR38.5 crore, with Q2 PAT of INR6 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 79% to INR254 crore, already about 84% of FY26 full-year revenue, with EBITDA of INR52.9 crore and net profit of INR38.5 crore versus INR6.5 crore in H1 FY26. Q2 revenue rose 61.7% YoY to INR140.6 crore, but Q2 EBITDA of INR12 crore (9% margin) and PAT of INR6 crore were well below Q1, which management attributed to a one-off strong Q1. Net worth rose 24% in six months to INR206.6 crore and debt-to-equity improved to about 1.6x from 1.7x. Management framed the company as a four-vertical group (equity investments, real estate, logistics, hospitality) shifting from marketing gains toward asset-backed income, with most asset revenues expected from FY28 onward.

segments.name: Equity investments / treasury
segments.commentary: Quoted equity investment of about INR230 crore, including stakes in Swiggy, TrucksUp and Drivers4Me. Management said these listed holdings are the most liquid source of funding for expansion.

segments.name: Real estate (Kolkata, OneWorld)
segments.commentary: 9.7% stake in OneWorld, a 212-acre Lucknow township, invested at about INR19.4 crore and revalued at INR153 crore (unrealised gain about INR134 crore). Kolkata plans 13.5 lakh sq ft of residential launches over 1-2 years; Alipore (Uma Properties) expected to yield about INR250 crore revenue, and Jessore Road JV (Elika Realestate, 45% stake) about INR1,100 crore over 5 years.

segments.name: Warehousing / logistics
segments.commentary: Dankuni, Delhi Road land with 40 lakh sq ft development potential and about INR600 crore capex, targeting 8-10% rental yields. Calcutta 100-125 acre project to deliver 25-30 lakh sq ft; revenue expected from calendar 2028. Visco Advisory warehousing asset sold for INR15.8 crore.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Acquired 33.33% of Blissara Resorts (Port Blair) with INR69 crore post-money valuation; planning a 140-key upper upscale hotel on 11 acres with coastal clearance in place. Construction to start in about a month; revenue expected from about 2030 with 5.5-7 year payback including debt and equity.

guidance_outlook: Blissara hotel: construction starting imminently, operations targeted in 2-2.5 years, revenue hitting top line by about 2030.
Warehousing (Calcutta): revenue expected from calendar 2028, within 1-1.5 years of securing land and approvals; leases under negotiation.
Uma Properties (Alipore residential): revenue expected from about March/April 2028, with a possible one-quarter delay.
Management expects constant revenue from most investments after the March 2028 quarter.

Management said the group will keep about 25% of its portfolio in liquid treasury such as equity markets, and expects construction funding and internal accruals to cover much of the next 3 years of spend.

Hotels targeted to be valued at INR500-600 crore each, with at least INR100 crore revenue per property; operator fee structure of about 2% base fee plus GOP-linked incentive, total under about 8-8.5% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Dankuni logistics land: 40 lakh sq ft development potential, capex about INR600 crore.
Calcutta: 13.5 lakh sq ft residential launches over 1-2 years; warehousing 100-125 acres giving 25-30 lakh sq ft immediate supply; construction started on ground.
Port Blair hotel: 140 keys on 11 acres; pipeline in Lucknow, Himachal and Ayodhya under evaluation.
Analyst estimate of INR900-1,500 crore funding need over 3-5 years was not disputed by management; funding to come from market borrowing, internal accruals, treasury and asset sales.
Nanak Logistics (63-acre park, Amazon anchor leasing 6.25 lakh sq ft on 20 acres) cited as prior group track record.
demand_pricing: Management cited zero Grade A warehouse supply in Calcutta and limited hotel supply in Port Blair, Lucknow, Himachal and Ayodhya; no pricing or occupancy data were given.
Warehouse targets: 8-10% rental yields, versus management's view that Tier 1 Grade A warehouses offer about 7-9% returns.
Hotel valuation benchmark cited at 10-16x EBITDA; 40-45% GOP assumed for the hotel.
Management said the Port Blair hotel faces no competition for about 3 years after opening.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company expand into factoring, lease financing and security-backed lending, and how does this fit with real estate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would be selective and pursue structured niche deals, not plain-vanilla lending, citing the Shalimar Lake City (OneWorld) revaluation and the Visco Advisory exit as examples.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical will create the most value over 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is most excited about hospitality, then warehousing, targeting INR100 crore revenue and INR500-600 crore valuation per hotel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for hospitality and warehousing revenue, and what are the execution risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Blissara revenue starts around 2030 after construction; warehousing revenue from calendar 2028; Alipore residential from about March/April 2028. Monsoon delays were the main constraint, now considered over.

qa_highlights.question: How does revenue recognition work with the hotel operator, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the operator takes a 1.5-2.5% base fee on gross revenue plus a share of gross operating profit, with total fees under about 8-8.5%. Payback is about 5.5-7 years including debt and equity; INR69 crore post-money valuation for Blissara.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR900-1,500 crore funding requirement be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will use the listed equity treasury (keeping about 25% liquid), market borrowing for construction, internal accruals, and asset liquidation as needed. Management did not confirm the analyst's INR400 crore liquidation estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Who owns the other 55% of the Jessore Road project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said three or four other West Bengal real estate developers hold the remaining 55%, chosen for execution capability.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter hospitality as landowner/investor rather than operator, and how much control does GAMCO have?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it lacks operating experience and prefers global operators, and that development-stage entry captures higher returns (11-12% on Tier 2 land versus 7-9% for Tier 1 warehouses). It said it would provide guidance and strategic input.

risks_watch: Q2 earnings fell sharply from Q1 (EBITDA INR12 crore vs INR41 crore; PAT INR6 crore vs INR32 crore), indicating lumpy income from investment gains.
Funding gap: analyst estimate of INR900-1,500 crore over 3-5 years versus debt of INR327 crore and debt-to-equity of 1.6x; reliance on market borrowing and asset sales.
Timelines are long: hotel revenue around 2030, warehousing from 2028, Alipore from 2028, with possible further slippage.
Heavy reliance on valuation gains (OneWorld INR134 crore unrealised gain) and on the listed equity book, which is market-sensitive.
Limited operating disclosure on the hotel and warehousing revenue models; stated targets are not yet backed by signed leases or contracts. Management said warehousing leases are being negotiated.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term asset plans, particularly hospitality and Calcutta warehousing. Management was less specific on near-term numbers, the Q2 profit decline and funding details, and it did not name the hotel operator or confirm the INR400 crore liquidation figure raised by an analyst.
key_quotes: So, the future of GAMCO cannot depend on a single segment.
Our consolidated revenue from operations grew 79% to INR254 crores, already about 84% of our revenue for the whole financial year '26.
We are not married to an industry. We are married to making capital for our investors.

growth.why: H1 FY27 revenue up 79% to INR254 crore, but Q2 EBITDA fell to INR12 crore (9% margin) from INR41 crore in Q1, and most new asset revenue (warehousing, hotel, Alipore) is deferred to 2028-2030 with only partial specifics (Dankuni INR600 crore capex, Calcutta under construction, Blissara hotel construction about to start) and no contracted orders behind it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 9% (INR12 crore) from INR41 crore in Q1, and management attributed Q1 to a one-off, so near-term margins are not guided higher.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Alipore residential (~INR250 crore revenue) is under construction with revenue from about March/April 2028, Calcutta warehousing (25-30 lakh sq ft) is under construction with revenue from calendar 2028, and Blissara hotel construction starts within about a month; all carry a possible one-quarter slip.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Most new asset revenue (warehousing, Alipore, hotel) is deferred to 2028-2030 and no signed leases are in place yet, while H1 FY27 revenue already rose 79% to INR254 crore on lumpy investment-linked income.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Dankuni logistics (INR600 crore capex, 40 lakh sq ft potential) is planned, hotel pipeline in Lucknow, Himachal and Ayodhya is under evaluation, and the analyst's INR900-1,500 crore 3-5 year funding need was not disputed by management.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 PAT fell to INR6 crore from INR32 crore in Q1 and management was less specific on near-term numbers, so no upgrade signal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Timelines are long and slippage is already flagged (Alipore possible one-quarter delay), and Q2 earnings fell sharply from Q1 with reliance on lumpy valuation gains (OneWorld INR134 crore unrealised) and the market-sensitive listed book.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Kolkata plans 13.5 lakh sq ft of residential launches over 1-2 years, and the Blissara 140-key hotel is approved with construction starting about a month after the call.

rows.label: Warehouse leases under negotiation (Calcutta)
rows.why: Management said Calcutta leases are being negotiated and zero Grade A warehouse supply exists there, but no signed leases were disclosed yet, against a 25-30 lakh sq ft target.

rows.label: Funding via treasury and asset sales
rows.why: Borrowings are INR327 crore at about 1.6x D/E, and management plans to fund the INR900-1,500 crore spend through listed equity (~INR230 crore), market borrowing and asset sales, but did not confirm the INR400 crore liquidation estimate.

rows.label: Jessore Road JV (Elika, 45% stake) revenue
rows.why: Management guided about INR1,100 crore of JV revenue over 5 years, with three or four other West Bengal developers holding the other 55%.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term hospitality and Calcutta warehousing plans and the INR1,100 crore Jessore JV, but cautious on near-term numbers, the Q2 profit drop, and funding details; analysts pushed on funding needs, the unnamed hotel operator and the INR400 crore liquidation estimate.
